sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section contains the opening header for the maamar, including the date of Shavuos night 1965.

translations.translation: B"S.
The first night of the festival of Shavuos
(towards morning),
the year 5725 (1965)

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section recounts the Talmudic narrative of Moshe ascending to heaven, the angels' objection to giving the Torah to man, and Moshe's responses regarding each commandment.

translations.translation: At the time that Moshe ascended to the heavens, the ministering angels said before the Holy One, blessed be He,
"Master of the Universe,
what is one born of a woman among us?"
He said to them, "He has come to receive the Torah."
They said before Him,
"A hidden treasure
[etc.] do You seek to give to flesh and blood? ... 'Place Your majesty upon the heavens.'"
The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moshe, "Give them an answer [etc.]."
[Moshe] said before Him,
"Master of the Universe,
the Torah that You are giving me, what is written in it?"
"'I am the L-rd your G-d who brought you out of the land of Egypt [etc.].'"
"Did you descend to Egypt? ... Why should the Torah be for you?"
"Again, what is written in it?"
"'You shall have no other gods.'"
"Do you dwell among nations that worship idolatry?"
"Again, what is written in it?"
"'Remember the Shabbos day to sanctify it.'"
"Do you perform work that you need rest?"
"Again, what is written in it?"
"'You shall not take [the L-rd's name in vain].'"
"Is there business dealings among you?"
"Again, what is written in it?"
"'Honor your father and your mother.'"
"Do you have a father and a mother?"
"Again, what is written in it?"
"'You shall not murder, you shall not commit adultery, you shall not steal.'"
"Is there jealousy among you? Is there an evil inclination among you?"
[And it can be said,
that in the response of Moshe Rabbeinu to the claim of the angels,
there are two matters in general.
"Did you descend to Egypt?" is a response regarding the entirety of the Torah,
for since the reason for the entire matter of the giving of the Torah is "I am the L-rd your G-d who brought you out of the land of Egypt,"
therefore,
since "did you descend to Egypt?"
(rhetorically)
"Why should the Torah be for you?"
And afterwards he adds "again, what is written in it,"
that also the specific commandments in the Torah
("You shall have no [other gods],"
"Remember the Shabbos day,"
etc.)
belong to Yisrael and not to the angels.]

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section raises questions about the angels' request and Moshe's responses, particularly regarding the commandments against murder, adultery, and theft.

translations.translation: And it must be understood,
that the request of the angels, "Place Your majesty upon the heavens," was that the Torah be given to them as it is in spirituality,
and what did Moshe answer them? "Do you perform work [that you need rest] etc."

Also, it must be understood what Moshe answered regarding the commandments "You shall not murder, you shall not commit adultery, you shall not steal": "Is there jealousy among you? Is there an evil inclination among you?"
For since the angels have no jealousy among them and they have no evil inclination, therefore there is no need to command and warn them about these commandments,
for seemingly it would have been better for him to say,
that also the commandments themselves
(as they are in physicality)
do not pertain to the angels
(as he said previously regarding the commandment of Shabbos,
"You shall not take [the L-rd's name in vain],"
and honoring father and mother).
